discovery: Prediction and discovery of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies, establishing a standard ruler for cosmic expansion

nominees.name: Rashid Sunyaev
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics, Garching, and Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University (Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian)

motivation: Sound waves in the primordial baryon-photon plasma leave a characteristic scale imprinted in the clustering of matter. Sunyaev (with the late Zel'dovich) predicted this relic in 1970. In 2005 Eisenstein, using SDSS luminous red galaxies, and Cole, leading the 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey analysis, independently detected the acoustic feature in galaxy clustering, confirming the gravitational growth of structure from CMB-era fluctuations. The BAO scale is calibrated by well-understood linear physics and is remarkably robust to systematics, making it a geometric standard ruler. It has since become a pillar of precision cosmology, and through BOSS, eBOSS and DESI it now provides some of the strongest tests of the nature of dark energy, including the recent hints of time-varying dark energy. Eisenstein's theoretical work also developed BAO into a practical cosmological probe. This is a discovery that reshaped how we measure the Universe.
